body.x: Surgeons learning robotic surgery need access to surgical consoles, but training time is limited. Meanwhile, valuable operating room recordings often end up on unsecured USB drives.

SofMedica Ventures, the investment and innovation division of the Greek-based MedTech distributor SofMedica Group, has built one platform for each problem. Managing Director Steven Gavas leads the company, which is exhibiting ERMIS VR and myDORA at KES 2026 and wants to speak with hospitals, training centers and MedTech distributors in Korea and the wider Asian market.

ERMIS VR is a digital twin of a robotic surgical console that runs on consumer VR headsets, so a surgeon can practice without an operating room or console time. A proprietary physics engine based on geometric algebra simulates tissue interactions and surgical instrument responses. Each training session also generates performance data. The company cites published findings showing up to a 30% reduction in time to proficiency, 58.8% fewer camera-related penalties and a 95% usability and acceptance score. It is designed for training and is not used to make clinical decisions during surgery.

myDORA, the Digital Operating Room Assistant, records full HD video directly from the endoscopic tower and runs in a browser on a laptop. It generates AI procedure summaries, responds to "Hey DORA" hands-free voice commands, supports live streaming for remote proctoring and technical support, and integrates with DICOM imaging workflows. Data is stored in encrypted, auditable European Union cloud storage that the company describes as GDPR- and EHDS-ready.

SofMedica was founded in 1994 in Romania and operates across Greece, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary, Croatia, Cyprus, Slovenia and Uzbekistan, with a network of more than 1,000 surgeons. The company says SofMedica Ventures' revenue grows at double digits each year, that myDORA is live in eight countries and that ERMIS VR is available in the United States, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia. It exports to the United Kingdom, the United States, South Korea and several European countries through distribution partners including ORamaVR and vr-expert.com.

SofMedica Ventures wants to expand distribution in the Middle East, South Korea and Australia and to find global strategic partners to help it reach key markets. It names providing round-the-clock support anywhere as its main difficulty, since it aims to match the service level it provides in its home market of Eastern Europe.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
